title: Move the CSRF token onto random_bytes and hash_equals
summary: Fix a guessable token and a loose check, then rename the key and make it single use.

files.content:
<?php

final class Csrf
{
    public function issue(): string
    {
        $token = md5(uniqid());
        $_SESSION['csrf'] = $token;

        return $token;
    }

    public function check(): bool
    {
        return $_POST['csrf'] == $_SESSION['csrf'];
    }
}

turns.user: review called the csrf token weak. src/Csrf.php. sort it out

assistant.body: md5(uniqid()) is built from the clock, so it is guessable. Let's take 32 bytes from random_bytes and hex them instead. hash_equals replaces the loose compare and keeps the comparison time independent of the input.

turns.user: calling check before anything was issued blows up though. same if the post has no key

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous version still assumed both keys were there. hash_equals raises a TypeError on anything that is not a string. Checking presence and type first turns a missing key into a plain false.

turns.user: the key name csrf collides with the other app on this host. call it csrf_token. and burn it once it passes

assistant.body: Renaming the key in one pass, then dropping it from the session the moment a check succeeds, so the same token cannot be replayed.
